gap: No result ChatGPT got states that how bright a laser looks equals its power times the eye's sensitivity at its wavelength. By the CIE 1988 photopic table, the eye's sensitivity is 0.710 at 520 nm and 0.885 at 532 nm (green) but 0.107 at 650 nm (red). That makes a green laser look about 6.6–8.3× brighter than a red laser of the same power. Because the laser class caps power (Class 2 at 1 mW, Class 3R at 5 mW), a green Class 3R laser can look about 5× brighter than a green Class 2 laser like the Klein 56074, and about 33× brighter than a 1 mW, 650 nm red Class 2 laser.
standout_why: I compared against our own page (dealectric.com/best-flashlight-with-laser-pointer, opened 2026-11-08). It says only that 'A red laser looks far dimmer to the eye than a green one of the same power' and that 'Only a Class 3R laser reads clearly in daylight'. It gives no number and no mechanism, and lists no laser wavelength. In the third chat, ChatGPT itself said green is 'generally easier to see', with no figure. I could not open the cited rival pages: Popular Mechanics' ArkPro Ultra review was blocked to the fetch tool and Yahoo Tech returned 403. The Klein 56074 maker page gives class and power (Class 2, <1 mW) but no wavelength and nothing on how bright it looks. None of the pages I could read combine the class power cap with the eye's wavelength sensitivity.
decides: This confirms that the main pick should be a green Class 3R light (the US Wuben X5 3R or the US Olight ArkPro) for anyone who wants to point at things at a distance or in daylight. The arithmetic: the 5 mW Class 3R cap × 0.710 = 3.55 brightness-weighted mW. A Class 2 green like the Klein 56074 (<1 mW) gives under 0.71, and a 1 mW, 650 nm red Class 2 gives 0.107. So ChatGPT's 'Best for work' Klein 56074 has at most a fifth of a 3R laser's visible brightness, and its red budget picks (Hyper Tough, Coast PM50R, Fenix E06R, Klein 56040) are far dimmer still. The same arithmetic means a Class 1 green at the 0.39 mW our page lists for the Wuben X5 Class 1 (0.39 × 0.710 = 0.277) would still look about 2.6× brighter than a 1 mW, 650 nm red. That gives the X5 Class 1 a sourced reason to rank above red lasers for workplaces that ban Class 3R.

Power cap for visible continuous-wave lasers by class
findings.note: Quoted: 'Class 2 lasers are limited to 1 mW continuous wave' and 'Visible continuous lasers in Class 3R are limited to 5 mW.' Class 2 relies on the blink reflex, which 'will limit the exposure to no more than 0.25 seconds'. Arithmetic: a 5 mW green at 520 nm gives 5 × 0.710 = 3.55 brightness-weighted mW, against 1 × 0.107 = 0.107 for a 1 mW red at 650 nm, about 33×.
